summary: Forest Service steel lookout on Topa Topa Peak, Ventura County, built 1938; cab burned in the 2006 Day Fire, steel tower remains; public access closed since 1959.

facts.design: Steel H-brace tower built to California Region 5 plan BC-301, with a wooden 14 by 14 foot C3 cab (cab since destroyed)
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Los Padres National Forest

access.note: Public access prohibited since the 1959 expansion of the Sespe Condor Sanctuary, per Carey (2012); no current Forest Service notice was checked

events.note: Built by the Forest Service; newspaper reported the station completed in October 1938
Dale Bever, a forestry student from Oregon, installed himself in the new lookout; the June 1939 newspaper said it was being used for the first time
Public access prohibited when the Sespe Condor Sanctuary was expanded
Day Fire reached the summit on September 16, 2006; the wooden cab burned and the steel tower survived
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on December 19, 2019

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 'Removed' entry (2006 Day Fire) refers to the wooden cab; the register also says the tower remains, so the steel tower stands and only the cab is gone

notes_for_editor: Height is disputed: the register and a July 1938 newspaper say 20 feet, a June 1939 newspaper and Carey's quote of a 1945 forest history say 30 feet. The record's height_m 9.1 matches the 30-foot figure and was left unchanged; it is not in facts. Access level 'closed' rests on Carey's 2012 post (public access prohibited since 1959); no current Forest Service notice was checked. The FFLA California list marks this site 'Standing*' and the meaning of the asterisk was not found. Newspaper quotes come from the Forest Lookouts compilation, not the original papers. Used 1 WebSearch and about 8 page reads, two over the per-tower budget, to get the access and height evidence.
